question: A test report ends with a figure that is 3 times the energy of a single launch, because 3 launches make a set. In one launch a carrier of 31 kg leaves the rail, and the energy of the launch is the energy the carrier holds because of its motion. Its launch speed in metres per second is built up as follows: take the value that the rate curve 2t^2 + 1t accumulates between t = 1 second and t = 3 seconds starting from zero at t = 1 second, subtract a slip loss of 11, multiply what remains by 8 for the eight-stage drive, and then subtract a friction loss of 9. The launch rail is 12 m long, a dimension the report never uses. What figure, in joules, ends the report?

A calibration log at a piston test cylinder lists two candidate acceleration readings, in meters per second squared, for a rocker arm: the two numbers add up to 7 and multiply together to give 10. Records confirm the true reading is the smaller of the two. Multiply that reading by 3, subtract 8 from the result, then add 8 back, then add 5 more. (The cylinder head is cooled by a fan drawing 15 watts, a detail that plays no role here.) That final acceleration acts on a rocker arm with a mass of 12,000 grams. What is the push this arm requires, in newtons?
Compute 2 times (2 plus 14). Add 8. A pump with mass 155 kilograms has this acceleration. Calculate force. Convert to kiloNewtons. Scale by 7. Subtract 7. What is the final force in kiloNewtons?

The sum 1 + 3 + 5 + 7 + 9 + 11 + 13 + 15 (2*k - 1 for k = 1 to 8) gives a velocity in m/s. A 31 kg object moving at this velocity stores energy. From this energy, 4 joules are subtracted. The result is scaled by 6, then by 7, and 7 joules are subtracted from the final value. A pressure of 1 atmosphere was noted but does not apply. What is the final energy in joules?

The number the warehouse supervisor wants is the total force in newtons for 9 identical conveyor lines, each with 4 identical pushers and a 7 N allowance for its end guard. Each pusher moves a 72 kg crate with an acceleration in metres per second squared equal to the greatest common divisor of 312 and 158. Find the force in newtons needed for one crate, multiply by 4 for the pushers on one line, and add the 7 N allowance. Multiply by 9 for all the lines. What is the total in N?
Find GCD of 293 and 324. A system with mass 52 kilograms has this velocity. Calculate kinetic energy. Convert to kiloJoules. Add 26. Scale by 11. What is the final energy in kiloJoules?

The last line of the log is 21 kJ more than 8 times the kilojoule reading described below. A launch controller adds its two dial settings 6 and 9, multiplies the sum by 3, and then subtracts 5 to fix the release speed in metres per second of a trolley whose mass is 13 kg. The trolley is released along a level rail and the energy it carries because of its motion is recorded. That energy, expressed in kilojoules, is the reading the line above is built from. The rail sits 0.75 m above the floor. What is the last line of the log, in kJ?

A toboggan centre's day figure is 10 times a single run's energy, expressed in kilojoules. A rider and sled together have a mass of 41000 g. Their speed, in metres per second, is built up as follows: twice the sum of the two gradient-dial readings, which are 6 and 8, then 19 subtracted, and the result multiplied by 5. What is the centre's day figure, in kJ?

A test loop's report ends with a number found by taking a certain kilojoule figure, subtracting 16 and then adding 8. That kilojoule figure is the kinetic energy of a 48 kg trolley on the loop, expressed in kilojoules. The trolley's speed in metres per second equals a certain accumulated meter total, minus 18. That accumulated total is what the loop's meter registers between the 3rd and the 4th second of a run, while the instantaneous rate it registers at time t seconds is 1 times t squared plus 2 times t. What number does the report end with, in kJ?

The total force in a lift-motor report, in N, is 9 times a single-motor figure. The single-motor figure is 6 N less than the force needed to accelerate an 84 kg cabin at a certain rate. That rate, in m/s², is found by taking the second derivative of y = 1·x³ - 5x² at x = 1, multiplying it by 3, and adding 24. What total does the report give, in N?
The combination C(8,3) = 56. Adding 1 gives 57 m/s^2. A 12 kg mass produces force = 684 N, decreased by 1, converted to kN. A limit is 10 kN. What is the final force in kN?

A spacecraft's reaction control system must produce thrust with 146 kg of propellant. At control state x = 1, the acceleration command follows 4x³ + 2x² m/s². The instantaneous acceleration is calculated, applied to the propellant mass via F = ma, then scaled by 11 hydraulic thrusters and converted to kN. The thrust is then amplified 8 times through feed-pressure stages and 5 times through nozzle configuration. What is the final achievable thrust in kN?

A calibration sheet at an elevator motor test rig lists two candidate acceleration readings, in meters per second squared, for a counterweight: the two numbers add up to 8 and multiply together to give 12. The correct reading is the larger of the two. That acceleration acts on a counterweight with a mass of 112 kilograms. (The elevator shaft is 18 meters tall, a fact that plays no role here.) Find the push this counterweight requires, in newtons, then convert that number into kilonewtons. Multiply the result by 11, then by 2, and then by 4. What is the final number, in kilonewtons?

A gymnastics rig report ends with one number in kilojoules. A trolley whose mass plate reads 12000 g runs along a beam at a speed, in metres per second, equal to the exact area under the curve y = 3x^2 + 5x between x = 1 and x = 2. The energy the moving trolley carries is the base value, and the report writes that in kilojoules. From the recorded value 26 is subtracted, in those same kilojoule units, as the rig's standing allowance. The hall contains 9 identical rigs, so the hall figure is 9 times the corrected value. What number ends the report, in kJ?

An equation x^2 - 12*x + 32 = 0 yields the smaller root as velocity in m/s. A 9 kg object moves at this velocity, storing energy. This energy is converted to kilojoules, multiplied by 11, multiplied by 2, and 30 kilojoules are subtracted. A sound level of 80 decibels was measured but does not apply. What is the final energy in kilojoules?

A vibration test applies load between positions x = 1 and x = 2 meters. The acceleration follows the integral of 3x² (giving 7 m/s² effective), applied to a 56 kg test mass producing force, converted to kN, reduced by 10 kN for baseline offset, then multiplied by 12 identical shakers running in parallel. The ambient sound level of 95 dB is not used. What is the total vibration force in kN?

On a robotic press, the rate at which the ram's acceleration changes follows j(t) = 3t² + 5t (in m/s³, t in seconds); between t = 1 s and t = 2 s, the net change in acceleration has 19 m/s² added to it. This total acceleration acts on the ram, whose mass is stated as 193000 grams. The resulting force is scaled by a factor of 6, then reduced by 26 N, and reduced again by 21 N. What is the final force, in newtons?

Sum from k=1 to 6 of k is 21 m/s² acceleration. With 155 kg, force = 3255 N, reduced by 30, scaled by 8, increased by 4, scaled by 12. The runtime is nodejs, not applicable. What is the final force in Newtons?

The final figure in a rocket-sled campaign report, in kN, is 27 kN of rail-brake load subtracted from a combined thrust expressed in kN. The combined thrust is that of 10 identical boosters acting together. Each booster supplies the force needed to accelerate a 190,000 g sled at a rate in m/s² equal to 5 times the sum of 2 and 14. What is the final figure, in kN?
Sum (2k - 1) for k from 1 to 7 equals 49 m/s. A 7 kg mass has kinetic energy scaled by 10, decreased by 23, converted to kJ. A reference is 100 m/s. What is the final energy in kJ?

A shipyard needs the total pull, in kilonewtons, on a winch gantry. The base rate a, in m/s^2, is the smaller value satisfying a^2 - 9a + 18 = 0, and the gearbox multiplies that base rate by 5. A control offset then adds 17 to the geared figure, giving the carriage's actual rate of change of speed in m/s^2. The carriage has a mass of 14000 g, and each winch supplies exactly the force needed to produce that motion. The gantry carries 9 identical winches working together. What total pull, in kN, does the gantry carry?

Compute 5 times (6 plus 2), yielding 40. A tank with mass 27 kilograms operates at this velocity. Calculate kinetic energy. Convert to kiloJoules. Scale by 7. Scale by 3. Subtract 6. What is the final energy in kiloJoules?

A press manufacturer needs the single ram rating in kN that closes its data sheet. The ram it drives has a mass of 57 kg. The ram acceleration in m/s^2 is the area under the curve 2*x**2 + 2*x between x = 2 and x = 4. The press stands 4 m tall, a figure on the sheet header that is not part of the rating. Once the force on the ram is known, 3 N is added for the return spring, and the total is expressed in kN. From that kN figure 13 is subtracted for the frame compliance credit. What ram rating in kN closes the data sheet?

A rotating shaft experiences variable torque. The torque rate follows 5x^3 + 2x^2 with first derivative at x = 1.0. A 64-kilogram rotor mass responds at this rate (in m/s²). Scale the force by 10, then by 4, add 4 kN, subtract 27 kN. The shaft diameter is 50 millimeters, not applicable. What is the final shaft torque in N?

At a model-rocket sled test track, a sled's position, in meters, follows s(t) = 3t^3 - 5t^2, where t is the time in seconds after launch. Engineers need how sharply the sled's motion is changing at t = 3 seconds. That value applies as the speed, in meters per second, of a sled with a mass of 38 kilograms. Find the energy this sled carries at that speed, in joules, then add 6 to that number, then subtract 17. Convert what remains into kilojoules, and then multiply the result by 3. What is the final number, in kilojoules?
